caption: The drawing depicts a symmetrical architectural facade with a central wooden door, painted in shades of brown, set in a rectangular wall. The wall is divided into three sections: the central section contains the door and is flanked by two arches, each outlined in blue with keystones and voussoirs, but the archways are filled in with a light color, suggesting no pass-through. The wall surface is decorated with floral and geometric patterns in red and blue. Above the door, there is an ornate horizontal panel showing blue vases with red floral decorations and a sunburst motif in the center. Vertical red decorative elements are positioned on either side of the door, within rectangular panels. Below the arches and around the door, lower wall panels feature a repeating motif of simple flowers with red petals and blue stems and leaves, each separated by vertical blue lines. The area immediately to the left and right of the door includes additional red abstract vine-like designs. The floor consists of reddish-brown rectangular tiles arranged in a regular pattern. The overall color scheme uses light blues, reds, and browns, and all elements are outlined with precise lines and washes of color.
title: Restoration Drawing
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
